newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index falls 1.1 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index falls 1.1 pct in August.

text.p: The Ferrell Fx Index fell 1.1 percent in August with the median return flat, Ferrell Capital Management said on Monday.
Fifteen of 34 programs reported positive results in August, Ferrell said.
Friedberg Commodity Management Inc, of Toronto, turned in the month's top performance, reporting gains of 8.7 percent.
"We remain long the New Zealand dollar and Czech koruna, two currencies that have been appreciating in response to their strong economies," Friedberg vice president Rick Zauderer told Ferrell.
London-based Chescor Ltd placed second in the survey, showing a rise of 4.2 percent, and Analytic TSA placed third with gains of 2.1 percent.
"Most traders who made money recently have been the ones who found more price change in the less-actively traded markets," said William Ferrell, president of Ferrell Capital Management.
For the 116-week period from January 1987 through August 1 996, the compounded annual return of the Ferrell FX Index is 17.4 percent.
The index provides a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 37 programs managed by 33 firms in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
